en.title: Polygon Patches Quiet Fork Flaws, Bitcoin Eyes Quantum Era, Insider Trading Fine
en.body:
Polygon deployed two hard forks this week to fix security flaws that were never publicly disclosed beforehand, raising fresh questions about transparency in protocol maintenance.

The Austin and Kyoto upgrades, rolled out on the Bor and Heimdall clients, addressed denial-of-service and consensus-hardening vulnerabilities. Polygon stated the issues were patched before any public disclosure and were never exploited, though the quiet nature of the fixes has drawn scrutiny from developers who argue that coordinated disclosure is standard practice for ecosystem safety.

Bitcoin moved closer to a post-quantum future this week, with developers refining signature schemes designed to withstand potential quantum computing threats. At the same time, Bernstein reaffirmed its bullish long-term outlook for the asset, projecting a cycle peak of $500,000, a forecast that has circulated widely among analysts despite ongoing volatility.

In a separate development, Solana validators agreed to cancel roughly 18.9 million SOL in staking rewards, a move aimed at curbing inflationary pressure on the network. The decision reflects growing governance attention to token economics as ecosystems balance growth incentives against supply discipline.

On the regulatory front, a former White House teleprompter operator was fined by the CFTC for insider trading tied to prediction markets. Gabriel Perez reportedly used advance access to speeches to bet on presidential mention contracts, profiting more than $107,500 before being caught. The case underscores expanding enforcement around market manipulation as crypto-linked derivatives attract closer oversight.

Market participants are weighing these developments against a backdrop of mixed price action. $BTC has traded in a relatively tight range, holding above key support near $80,000 while facing resistance around $85,000. $ETH remains pressured below $3,000, and $SOL has dipped following the reward cancellation announcement, though on-chain activity suggests long-term holder conviction remains intact. Trading volumes across major venues have stabilized compared with earlier in the week.
